root_cause: When Curl_ssl_scache_take() was reworked to add QUIC 0RTT support and richer trace logging, the call to Curl_ssl_scache_unlock(data) was placed immediately after the critical section that removes/takes a session from the peer's session list, but before the subsequent trace-logging code that itself reads the same shared peer->sessions list (via Curl_llist_count) to report the remaining session count. This left a window where lock-protected data is read/used without holding the lock.
findings: In Curl_ssl_scache_take(), the SSL session cache lock is released via Curl_ssl_scache_unlock(data) before the trace logging code runs. The trace statement (CURL_TRC_CF / later CURL_TRC_SSLS) calls Curl_llist_count(&peer->sessions) to report how many sessions remain for that peer.
